outcome: Not settled in general since 26 January 2024. In-window work is of three kinds: refinements of the exact formula for Brumer-Stark units that underlies the totally real case (Honnor revisions of Jan 2024 and Dec 2025; Dasgupta-Honnor-Spiess, JLMS Oct 2025), a May 2025 Caltech talk claiming an exact formula is proved (not traced to a written argument), and conjectural or restricted results (Morain on one-complex-place fields; Morton on imaginary quadratic fields; Kopp, Yalkinoglu, Sprehe, Nikolaev on real quadratic cases). No in-window event credits an AI system.
problem_asks: Statement: extend the Kronecker-Weber theorem (every abelian extension of Q lies in a cyclotomic field, i.e. is generated by roots of unity) to any base number field. Parts: (1) for an arbitrary number field K, the abelian extensions of K, including the maximal abelian extension K^ab; (2) an explicit description of them, meaning generators rather than a bare existence statement; (3) generators of the kind Kronecker and Hilbert had in mind: analogues of roots of unity, i.e. special values of suitable analytic (transcendental) functions, as in the CM case over imaginary quadratic fields; (4) the statement names no restriction to totally real, CM, or real or imaginary quadratic base fields, so each such restricted case is a case of the problem and not the whole of it.

events.what_happened: Samit Dasgupta (Duke) and Mahesh Kakde (IISc) posted arXiv:2103.02516 (v1 titled, per search snippet of the v1 PDF, 'Brumer-Stark Units and Hilbert's 12th Problem'; v2 25 Jul 2023 titled 'Brumer-Stark Units and Explicit Class Field Theory'). Abstract: for a totally real field F of degree n and odd prime p, they prove the p-part of the integral Gross-Stark conjecture for Brumer-Stark p-units in CM abelian extensions of F; the Brumer-Stark units together with n-1 further easily described elements (square roots of certain elements of F) generate the maximal abelian extension of F, which the abstract presents as unconditional and as involving p-adic integration for infinitely many primes p. Published as Duke Math. J. 173(8), 1477-1555 (DOI 10.1215/00127094-2023-0039), listed Jan 2024. Duke news (1 June 2021) and Quanta (25 May 2021, per snippet) reported the preprint in 2021.
events.revisions: v2 25 Jul 2023 (retitled); journal version Duke Math. J. 173(8) 2024 (Duke Scholars lists publication date 1 Jan 2024).
events.delivers: For totally real base fields only: an unconditional generating set (Brumer-Stark units plus n-1 square roots) for the maximal abelian extension of any totally real field F, via the p-part of the integral Gross-Stark conjecture for odd primes p. Restrictions: base field totally real; generators are p-adic in nature (Wikipedia's Modern developments section calls it a p-adic solution); the exact formula for the units was only up to a bounded root-of-unity factor at the time (per the 2023 Honnor abstract); the abstract's p-adic result is stated for odd p.
events.remains: The problem for arbitrary base number fields (not only totally real ones); the complex-analytic special-value form Hilbert had in mind; the exact root-of-unity-free formula for the units (addressed by Honnor, below).

The exact formula was stated only up to a bounded root-of-unity factor in the versions read (per the Honnor 2023 abstract). No error in the 2021 generation theorem was identified in any source read.

The generators are p-adic special values rather than complex-analytic ones, so whether this counts as the problem's form is for the later pass.
events.object: Brumer-Stark units (p-units in CM abelian extensions of a totally real field F, defined from Stickelberger-type elements), together with n-1 explicit square roots of certain elements of F. They generate the maximal abelian extension of F. The units are given by a p-adic analytic formula, which the paper states only up to a bounded root of unity in the version read. Explicit generators, not an existence proof.

Abstract: 'We prove this conjecture away from p=2, that is, after tensoring with Z[1/2]', and a stronger version conjectured by Kurihara, giving the 0th Fitting ideal of the minus part of the T-smoothed class group in terms of Stickelberger elements. Published as Annals of Math. 197(1), 289-388 (2023), per search snippet of the Annals listing, which was not opened.

events.remains: The prime 2 at the time of this paper (later addressed by Dasgupta-Kakde-Silliman-Wang, Oct 2023); everything in the problem statement.

events.direction: Cuts toward the Brumer-Stark conjecture (true away from 2 by this paper). It is about annihilation of class groups, a different question from generation of abelian extensions, though it is the algebraic engine of the totally real construction.

events.what_happened: Matthew H. L. Honnor, 'On the Root of Unity Ambiguity in a Formula for the Brumer-Stark Units', arXiv:2302.12332. Abstract, verbatim: 'We prove a conjectural formula for the Brumer-Stark units.' 'Dasgupta-Kakde have shown the formula is correct up to a bounded root of unity.' 'In this paper we resolve the ambiguity in their result.' 'We also remove an assumption from Dasgupta-Kakde's result on the formula.' Theorem 2.7 (v3 HTML) states that under condition (5) (p odd, and H intersect F(mu_{p^infinity}) contained in H+), the formula holds with no root-of-unity ambiguity, establishing the Dasgupta-Spiess Conjecture 2.5. The removed assumption is condition (4) (a prime in S, unramified in H, with Frobenius complex conjugation).
events.revisions: v2 11 Jan 2024 (in window); v3 17 Dec 2025 (in window). The v2 comment reads 'This version proves a stronger result, dealing with the ambiguity at 2'. That comment appears on the default abstract page and on the v2-specific page, so it is not certain which version carries it.
events.delivers: Removes the root-of-unity ambiguity from the Dasgupta-Kakde exact formula for Brumer-Stark units in CM extensions of totally real fields, under condition (5) (p odd and a stated condition on H), and removes one of Dasgupta-Kakde's assumptions. Whether the ambiguity at 2 is removed is stated only in the version comment, which is ambiguous as to version. Restricted to Brumer-Stark units; does not by itself give generators for arbitrary base fields.
events.remains: The problem for arbitrary base number fields; cases excluded by condition (5); the general generation question.
events.time_since_posted: About 3 years 8 months since v1; v3 about 10 months ago. No journal reference shown on the arXiv page.
events.doubts: No journal reference or referee record found. The abstract's first sentence ('We prove a conjectural formula') reads oddly for a result the paper states as a theorem. The abstract page does not say whether the ambiguity at 2 is removed in v2 or only in v3. No independent engagement was found in the searches run here.
events.direction: Cuts toward an exact, root-of-unity-free formula for Brumer-Stark units under stated conditions, strengthening the totally real construction. It does not change whether the problem as stated is settled.
events.object: A formula for the Brumer-Stark units in CM extensions H of a totally real field F, exact with no root-of-unity ambiguity under conditions (p odd; H intersect F(mu_{p^infinity}) contained in H+). It is a formula, not an existence statement.

events.what_happened: Nicolas Bergeron, Pierre Charollois and Luis E. Garcia, 'Elliptic units for complex cubic fields (on Eisenstein's Jugendtraum)', arXiv:2311.04110. They conjecture that complex numbers built from the elliptic gamma function are units in narrow ray class fields of a complex cubic field, with a Shimura-style reciprocity law for the Galois action; they support this with numerical evidence and prove a Kronecker limit formula. The authors present it as a contribution to Hilbert's 12th problem for complex cubic fields.
events.revisions: v2 30 Nov 2023 (minor changes, updated references).
events.delivers: Conjectures for complex cubic fields (units and reciprocity law); a proven Kronecker limit formula. Restricted to complex cubic fields.
events.remains: The unit and reciprocity conjectures; all other base fields.
events.time_since_posted: About 2 years 11 months.
events.directly_checkable: Numerical values of the elliptic gamma construction for specific cubic fields, per the authors' numerical evidence; not checked here.
events.doubts: Conjectural, supported by numerical evidence only.
events.direction: Conjectural, pointing toward explicit elliptic units generating ray class fields of complex cubic fields.

events.what_happened: Pierre L. L. Morain, 'Elliptic Units Above Fields With Exactly One Complex Place', arXiv:2406.06094. Constructs geometric variants of multiple elliptic Gamma functions with transformation properties under SL_d(Z) (d >= 2), evaluates them at points of degree-d fields with exactly one complex place, and conjectures that the infinite products yield algebraic units in abelian extensions tied to conjectural Stark units; numerical support for cubic, quartic and quintic fields. The abstract says 'we conjecture that such infinite products yield algebraic units in abelian extensions of' K.
events.revisions: v2 19 Dec 2024 (more precise conjecture, new numerical examples). Superseded by arXiv:2601.11961 per that paper's comments.
events.delivers: Conjecture only: that the values give algebraic units in abelian extensions of fields with exactly one complex place of degree d >= 3, supported numerically in degrees 3-5. No theorem.
events.remains: All of the problem: the conjecture itself, all base fields outside the one-complex-place class, and the proof of any generation statement.

events.what_happened: Bora Yalkinoglu, 'A note on Shintani's invariants', arXiv:2408.07309. Expresses Shintani's invariants (defined by the double sine function) through q-Pochhammer symbols, generalising Yamamoto's observation, for real quadratic fields with a given fundamental unit. The abstract states that these invariants are conjectured to generate abelian extensions of real quadratic fields, which would address Hilbert's 12th problem in that setting. The fetched abstract page describes the generation result as a conjecture and does not explicitly say it is open; the note proves no generation statement.
events.revisions: v2 6 Aug 2025; v3 6 Feb 2026 (comment: 'accepted final version, some improvements').
events.delivers: Formulas for Shintani's invariants in q-Pochhammer terms, for real quadratic fields. It is an identity about the invariants, not a generation statement.
events.remains: Shintani's conjecture that the invariants generate abelian extensions of real quadratic fields; all other base fields.
events.time_since_posted: About 26 months; none found in the searches run here.

events.what_happened: Patrick Morton, 'A proof of Sugawara's conjecture on Hasse-Weber ray class invariants', arXiv:2406.11479. States a proof of Sugawara's 1936 conjecture: a ray class field of conductor f over an imaginary quadratic field K is generated over K by one primitive f-division value of the tau-function (Weber's function, modified by Hasse). Abstract: 'a proof is given of Sugawara's conjecture from 1936'.
events.revisions: v2 21 Aug 2024; v3 26 Aug 2024; v4 11 Mar 2025 (added a case in Section 6.2); v5 2 Jun 2026 (corrections to Section 6.2, appendix added; 81 pages).
events.delivers: For imaginary quadratic base fields only: one-generator description of ray class fields by a single tau-value, claimed for all conductors f != 1 (abstract). Within the imaginary quadratic case, where CM theory already solved the problem (Hasse 1927, Deuring 1958), this is a sharper form of a settled case. The visible text of the introduction states the main theorem without qualification, but the body restricts some cases (for example d_K not equal to -3, -4 and congruence conditions on d_K), and the full text was not read to confirm every case.
events.remains: Every base field other than imaginary quadratic fields; the general problem.
events.time_since_posted: About 2 years 4 months; journal publication not found in the searches run here.
events.doubts: Corrections were issued in v4 and v5 to Section 6.2, and a case was added in v2. The visible text restricts some cases; the body was truncated in the read (about 100k of 135k characters), so the coverage of all cases could not be confirmed. Sugawara's own partial results and the ideal-case results of Jung, Koo, Shin and Yoon (search snippets, not opened) are earlier partial work on the same conjecture.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture as stated (a claimed proof). It concerns a settled case of the problem, so it changes nothing for the general problem.
events.object: Not an object exhibited. The generator is a primitive f-division value of Weber's tau-function (Hasse's modified form) for the ray class.

events.what_happened: Gene S. Kopp, 'The Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle: Stark units from q-Pochhammer ratios', arXiv:2411.06763. Reinterprets Stark units of real quadratic fields as values of a modular cocycle at real multiplication points, and proves a refinement of Shintani's Kronecker limit formula (Theorem 1.1, an identity expressing a Stark class invariant through the cocycle). Its abelian-extension statements are conditional: Theorem 1.3(1) assumes Conjecture 6.9; Conjecture 1.4 is stated but not proved.
events.delivers: An unconditional limit formula for Stark units of real quadratic fields via the Shintani-Faddeev cocycle. Generation of abelian extensions is conditional on Conjecture 6.9 (per Theorem 1.3, as read); unconditional for no extension statement.
events.remains: The unconditional generation statement (Conjecture 6.9 and 1.4); all base fields other than real quadratic ones.
events.time_since_posted: About 23 months; none found in the searches run here.
events.direction: Partly positive (an identity for Stark units of real quadratic fields); generation remains conditional, so it does not move the problem's status.

events.what_happened: Igor V. Nikolaev, 'Addendum to Measured foliations and Hilbert 12th problem', arXiv:2505.22272. Studies numerical examples of abelian extensions of real quadratic fields, building on the 2008 paper. Its Theorem 1 (attributed to Hecke): for each prime p = 3 mod 4 there is a Hecke eigenform f in S_2(Gamma(p)) with the ring class field of Q(sqrt(-p)) contained in K_f. Theorem 3: for each level N > 1 there is a real quadratic field whose ring class field mod some conductor lies in K_f. Theorem 4 (the author's addition): the analogue at level m^2 p. Remark 2: 'A rigorous proof of these inclusions is unknown to the author.' Computations use LMFDB, numbertheory.org, PARI/GP and Magma, and some entries exceeded LMFDB/Magma capacity.
events.revisions: v1 only.
events.delivers: Inclusions of class fields into Hecke-eigenform fields, claimed by the author for numerical examples; the author says the inclusions are not rigorously proved. Not a generation result for an arbitrary base field.
events.remains: Everything in the problem; the rigorous inclusions (per Remark 2).

events.what_happened: Pierre L. L. Morain, 'Geometric families of multiple elliptic Gamma functions and arithmetic applications, I', arXiv:2510.16515. A framework for applying multiple elliptic Gamma functions to Hilbert's 12th problem over number fields with exactly one complex place, extending a rank-3 construction of Felder, Henriques, Rossi and Zhu to higher rank. The introduction states theorems on the modular property and equivariance (Theorem 1), a cocycle relation (Theorem 2), and partial zeta values at s=0 for totally real fields (Theorem 3). The elliptic-unit construction itself is deferred to later papers.

Shows that smoothed versions of the functions yield partial modular symbols for congruence subgroups of SL_n(Z), restricting to (n-2)-cocycles on tori from totally positive units, and that the smoothed Bernoulli rational functions reduce to smoothed higher Dedekind sums with bounded denominators.

events.what_happened: Soren Sprehe, 'Antisymmetry of real quadratic singular moduli', arXiv:2603.09764. Proves a conjecture of Darmon and Vonk on the antisymmetry of real quadratic singular moduli, by analysing rigid meromorphic cocycles for the orthogonal group of a quaternion algebra, following Darmon-Gehrmann-Lipnowski. Also proves modularity of a generating series of Kudla-Millson divisors.

events.remains: The general conjecture that rigid meromorphic cocycle values at real multiplication points lie in composita of abelian extensions of real quadratic fields (Darmon-Vonk program); the problem.

events.direction: Proves a specific conjectured identity in the Darmon-Vonk programme; does not settle the problem as stated.

Proves conjectures of Giampietro and Darmon on factoring a ratio of CM-values of p-adic theta-functions on a genus-zero Shimura curve, a p-adic analogue of Gross-Zagier's work on differences of singular moduli. Two proofs: algebraic (CM theory) and analytic (p-adic deformations of Hilbert Eisenstein series). Search snippets say the thesis was defended at Leiden on 30 Oct 2024 (not opened).

disputes.summary: Whether the exact formula for Brumer-Stark units is proved. The May 2025 Caltech abstract (Dasgupta) says a newly proven exact formula, unrestricted by p=2. The 2023 Honnor abstract says the formula holds only up to a bounded root of unity in Dasgupta-Kakde; Honnor's own v2/v3 (in window) claims to remove the ambiguity under condition (5). The write-up behind the 2025 talk was not identified.

Whether the version comment 'proves a stronger result, dealing with the ambiguity at 2' belongs to Honnor v2 (Jan 2024) or v3 (Dec 2025). The default abstract page and the v2-specific page both show it, so the version carrying the claim is not certain.

Scope of the 2021 Dasgupta-Kakde result against the problem: the generators are p-adic and exist for totally real base fields only. Wikipedia's Modern developments section says the authors 'announced a p-adic solution'. Whether that counts as the problem's form is for the later pass.

summary: Found: no event since 26 January 2024 settles Hilbert's twelfth problem as stated. The Simons Foundation's June 2026 status article (Hilbert's 23 problems at ICM 2026) gives entry 12 as 'Status: Unresolved', and Wikipedia (last edited 13 April 2026) says the general case is open, with the complete answer worked out only for Q and imaginary quadratic fields and the totally real case credited to Dasgupta-Kakde. The main older result is Dasgupta-Kakde (arXiv 3 March 2021; Duke Math. J. 173(8), 2024), which for totally real base fields gives an unconditional generating set (Brumer-Stark units plus n-1 square roots) for the maximal abelian extension, with p-adic methods and odd primes. It predates the window and is recorded as an event. In-window work falls in three groups. (i) Refinements of the explicit formula for Brumer-Stark units behind the totally real case: Honnor's preprint (first posted Feb 2023) was revised on 11 Jan 2024 and 17 Dec 2025 and claims to remove the root-of-unity ambiguity under stated conditions; Dasgupta-Honnor-Spiess (JLMS, Oct 2025) shows three conjectural formulas agree; and a May 2025 Caltech talk by Dasgupta claims 'a newly proven exact formula', which I could not trace to a written argument, so it is recorded as an open dispute. (ii) Conjectural elliptic-unit constructions for fields with exactly one complex place (Morain: conjecture June 2024, framework Oct 2025, simplified conjecture Jan 2026, numerical checks in degrees 3-6); these are conjectures, not theorems, and the 2024 Bergeron-Charollois-Garcia conjecture for cubic fields predates the window. (iii) Restricted or conditional results that do not reach the general problem: Morton's claimed proof of Sugawara's conjecture (imaginary quadratic fields only, revised through June 2026, no journal found); Yalkinoglu and Kopp on Shintani invariants and Stark units of real quadratic fields (formula identities, generation conditional or conjectural); Sprehe's proof (March 2026) of a Darmon-Vonk antisymmetry conjecture for real quadratic singular moduli; and Nikolaev's 2008 claim of Manin's real quadratic conjecture with its 2025 addendum, whose Remark 2 says a rigorous proof of the inclusions it uses is unknown to its author. Close calls: whether the p-adic totally real result counts as settling part of the problem; whether Honnor's formula plus the 2021 generation theorem makes the totally real case explicit in the sense the problem asks; and whether the Caltech 2025 exact-formula claim is correct, which depends on arXiv versions I could read only through summaries. AI: explicit AI searches were run (the problem name with AI, LLM, Claude, Gemini, GPT and AlphaProof terms; AI-result trackers; the Erdos and FrontierMath benchmarks; the OpenAI 6 October 2026 release of 719 manuscripts, whose full CONTENTS.md I read in segments and which contains no family on this problem). No source opened credits an AI system with any step on this problem, and no readable acknowledgement or contribution statement in the in-window papers names one, so none_found is true for every event. Adjacent but not this bullet: a May 2026 OpenAI unit-distance disproof is reported in secondary coverage to use class field tower tools, and an October 2026 arXiv preprint (2608.31162) on trinomial containment is about Hilbert's tenth problem; neither was opened or recorded as an event here.
competing_reading: Read the 2021 Dasgupta-Kakde result, together with Honnor's exact formula and the 2025 talk's claim, as a substantial resolution of the totally real case: it gives an unconditional, explicit generating set for every abelian extension of every totally real field, which is the Kronecker-Weber-type answer Hilbert asked for in that class. On that reading the in-window refinements take the case from 'explicit up to a root of unity' to 'explicit', and the problem is settled for totally real fields. The opposing reading: the generators are p-adic, exist only for totally real base fields, and do not give the complex-analytic special values of Kronecker's Jugendtraum that the problem names; the Wikipedia article itself says the complete answer is worked out only for imaginary quadratic fields. On that reading no in-window event changes the status of the problem as stated, and the one-complex-place results are conjectures with no proof.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Duke Math. J. 2024 text of Dasgupta-Kakde, and Honnor's arXiv v2 and v3 full texts with their hypothesis lists, to confirm the exact formula and where the ambiguity at 2 is removed. (2) The write-up, if any, behind the May 2025 Caltech talk's 'newly proven exact formula'. (3) A journal acceptance or independent verification of Morton's proof (arXiv:2406.11479) and of Honnor's preprint (arXiv:2302.12332). (4) A readable full text of Nikolaev's 2008 paper (arXiv:0804.0057 v9) to check whether its proof depends on the inclusions that the 2025 addendum's Remark 2 says are unproven. (5) For AI involvement: an acknowledgement or contribution statement in any of these papers naming a system; none of the readable texts contains one. (6) A check of the Lean or mathlib status of a Kronecker-Weber or class-field-theory formalisation for this problem, which was not done here and would not decide the status.

judgement.why: The statement asks for a Kronecker-Weber analogue over any number field, so restricted base-field classes are cases. Dasgupta-Kakde 2021 (pre-snapshot, Duke Math. J.) settles the totally real case with explicit generators: case, digested, witness. Nikolaev 2008 is a pre-snapshot claimed real quadratic case, journal-published but doubtful. After the snapshot, nothing settles a new case: the Morain, Kopp, Yalkinoglu and Black items are conjectures, frameworks or identities (none). Morton's Sugawara proof sharpens the imaginary quadratic case, which CM theory already settled, into a single-generator statement, so it is a variant. Sprehe proves a Darmon-Vonk identity, also a variant. The Honnor and Dasgupta-Honnor-Spiess refinements, and the 2025 Caltech talk, make the units formula exact within the totally real case that was already settled before the snapshot, so they add no new scope (none). Brumer-Stark and Gross-Stark results answer different conjectures. No event credits an AI system.
judgement.doubts: Honnor's revisions (v2 Jan 2024, v3 Dec 2025) might carry new mathematics, namely the ambiguity at 2. Even if they do, they refine a case that was already settled and do not change the scope. Whether p-adic generators count as Hilbert's intended form is debatable; I treated the totally real result as a case either way.
